engine: infer/rtrvc.py (the streaming engine realtime_gui.py ships with, NOT used by rvc_service today)
method: torch.cuda.synchronize() around RVC.infer(), same RVC object reused across configs (last_rvc=), 9 sequential blocks per config with the first 2 dropped (cache fill-in / first-call model loads)
reading: Per-call cost is roughly flat (~110-130ms) across this whole block_time/extra_time range, because F0 is cached incrementally (only the new block is re-estimated, infer/rtrvc.py:281-296) and the vocoder only decodes `return_length` samples via skip_head (infer/module/models.py SynthesizerTrnMs768NSFsid.infer), not the whole window. extra_time (history context) barely moves the cost -- block_time is the only real lever, and 0.25-0.4s leaves 2-4x real-time margin on this GPU, vs. the offline pipeline's ~350ms floor. At block=0.15s the margin (rtf=0.73) is thin for a 4GB Pascal card and not recommended as a first target.
